title: Conclusion
coreMove: Treat depth as a life design choice that must be chosen repeatedly, not as a single productivity tactic.
sourcePressure: The source frame supports a narrow closing case around Bill Gates and the value of a deep life.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version summarizes the rules; the chapter must make the reader decide what a deep life would require in practice.

exampleSpecs.domain: a senior public-health modeler choosing her next five-year role
exampleSpecs.audience: an experienced professional deciding whether her work life supports depth
exampleSpecs.stakes: she may accept a title-heavy role that removes the modeling work she does best
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the prestigious role with the quieter role by counting which one preserves weekly model-building depth
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two offer letters beside a calendar marked with model-building blocks

exampleSpecs.domain: a small-town newspaper publisher rebuilding the reporting calendar
exampleSpecs.audience: a leader deciding whether the organization can live by depth instead of churn
exampleSpecs.stakes: local accountability reporting dies if every day is filled with quick briefs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he removes three low-value recurring briefs and assigns one reporter a protected investigation block every week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a newsroom budget board with three recurring briefs crossed out

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate architecture student designing a thesis year
exampleSpecs.audience: a student turning the rules into a full-year operating choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: the thesis becomes a collage of quick references unless she protects long design sessions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places studio depth, tool limits, boredom training, and shallow-work caps onto one weekly template
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a thesis pin-up wall beside a blank weekly template

exampleSpecs.domain: a union training coordinator redesigning apprenticeship study time
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator moving from tips to institutional habits
exampleSpecs.stakes: apprentices pass safety modules but fail complex diagnostic work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed diagnostic exam, he redesigns the schedule so apprentices practice hard fault analysis before routine paperwork
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a failed diagnostic rubric beside an apprenticeship rotation chart

exampleSpecs.domain: a climate-litigation team planning a year of expert discovery
exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead translating a deep-life principle into team operating norms
exampleSpecs.stakes: expert arguments weaken if the year dissolves into reactive filings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks each attorney to name the one deep contribution the case needs, then builds the year around those blocks before deadlines are added
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an expert-discovery timeline printed across a conference table

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice music therapist deciding what kind of practice to keep
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner measuring a deep life by attention quality rather than public status
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients receive thin, familiar routines if she stops learning difficult repertoire
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses a smaller caseload that preserves daily repertoire study and writes the tradeoff plainly before accepting it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked songbook beside a caseload schedule on a clinic desk

skillTargets: integrate the four rules into a whole-life choice
evaluate tradeoffs that preserve or destroy depth
distinguish a deep life from isolated productivity tactics
apply the supported Bill Gates closing idea without expanding into unsupported biography

tryThisNowSpec: Write one tradeoff you would have to accept for a deeper work life, then name the concrete weekly block that tradeoff protects.
